title: Kernel-aware routing and pad-elision batcher
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We observe significant wasted GPU cycles and memory due to padding-heavy micro-batches when serving variable-length requests. Existing length-bucketing reduces some waste, but kernel incompatibilities and prefill/decode scheduling still force conservative padding. This ticket designs and implements a kernel-aware routing layer combined with a pad-elision batcher that dynamically coalesces requests into micro-batches aligned to kernel-friendly seqlen groups and opportunistically elides padding during prefill when KV cache alignment allows. The goal is to reduce average tokens-per-GPU by 12-30% on tail-heavy workloads while keeping 99th percentile latency within current SLOs.
proposal: 1) Introduce a kernel capability registry that encodes preferred sequence length multiples and supported attention optimizations per kernel build (e.g., 64, 128 strides, fused rotary vs unfused). 2) On request ingest, annotate requests with sequence-length, prefill flag, and kernel affinity hints. 3) Routing layer groups inflight requests into candidate buckets by kernel affinity and near sequence length, then runs a pad-elision pass: if prefix KV caches are compatible and transformer block alignment is satisfied, elide zero-padding and mark partial-KV slots. 4) Micro-batcher will emit packing metadata so runtime can run decode across heterogeneous KV layouts (fallback to conservative padding if mismatched). 5) Telemetry and safety net: continuous latency spike detector with automatic fallback to safe padding for affected routes.
design_notes:
- Kernel capability registry is a small protobuf table persisted in node-local config and reconciled from central model profiles.
- Affinity heuristic: prioritize kernel with lowest estimated cycles/token given seqlen and model variant.
- Pad-elision constraints: only when prefill batch contains identical model weights, identical rotary/position config, and when the target decode kernel supports partial-KV offsets.
- Metadata plumbing: extend RequestContext with flat annotations: seqlen_str, prefill_bool, kernel_tag. No nested protos in ticket JSON.
- Backward compatibility: if downstream runtime lacks partial-KV support, registry advertises support=false and batcher falls back to existing bucketing + padding.
tradeoffs:
- Complexity vs benefit: introduces additional routing logic and metadata plumbing which increases code surface and potential for regressions. However, expected cost savings and throughput gains on production tail-heavy traffic justify the work.
- Telemetry vs privacy: per-request affinity logging required for analysis; log retention must obey PII/data policies.
- Edge cases: small burst traffic might be delayed slightly due to grouping window (trade latency for batch efficiency). We'll expose a per-route knob to limit grouping window to keep interactive routes low-latency.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): implement registry + passive telemetry in dev cluster, no pad-elision, just collect affinity recommendations (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (small canary): enable pad-elision for non-critical routes with 5% traffic, monitor GPU utilization, per-route p99 latency and error rates (3 weeks).
Phase 3: progressive ramp to 50% then 100% across compatible clusters, add automatic fallback on latency regression (2-4 weeks).
Rollback: global switch in config center to disable pad-elision and routing affinity instantly.
metrics: Primary: tokens_per_gpu_hour (expected -12% to -30% on target workloads). Secondary: p50/p95/p99 latency delta, error_rate, scheduling_delay distribution, kernel_mismatch_count. Observability: dashboard with per-route kernel affinity heatmaps and pad-savings over time.
test_plan: Unit tests for registry parsing and affinity heuristics. Integration tests: simulate mixed seqlen traffic and assert batch composition and kernel selection decisions. Perf benchmarks on staging with synthetic tails (log-normal seqlen) to measure tokens/GPU and latency. Chaos test: force kernel capability flip mid-batch and verify fallback correctness. Add e2e test that validates decode correctness when partial-KV offsets are used.
